title: Letter from Gull Rock
genre: a lighthouse keeper's letter to family
paras: Dear Margaret,

Winter has come early to Gull Rock. The lamp still burns green, as it did in Father's day; every sailor on this coast knows a green light means Gull Rock and no other. I climb the ninety-nine steps to tend it three times a night. Father used to say ninety-nine steps kept a keeper humble.

The supply boat comes each Tuesday. This week it arrived on [[Thursday|Tuesday|The boat comes "each Tuesday", and this visit was "as usual".]], as usual, with flour, lamp oil and your letter. Old Tom, who rows it, says the harbour froze last week for the first time in thirty years.

On Friday the fog came in so thick that I lit the [[red|green|The lamp burns green, and "a green light means Gull Rock and no other". There is no red lamp.]] lamp an hour early. Coming down afterwards I counted the steps, as I always do: [[eighty-nine|ninety-nine|The tower has ninety-nine steps (mentioned twice), and the count was "same as ever".]], same as ever. Biscuit was asleep by the stove when I got in.

Give my love to the children, and tell little Anne her [[grandfather|uncle|William signs as Margaret's brother, and they share a father, so he is Anne's uncle, not her grandfather.]] has not forgotten her birthday.
Your loving brother,
William

title: Incident Report, Halvorsen Museum
genre: a museum night guard's incident report
paras: Filed by night guard Ruth Okafor, 4 June.

I began my rounds at 22:00 in the East Wing, as the schedule requires. The East Wing holds the clock collection; the West Wing holds the paintings. At 23:15 I heard glass break somewhere to the [[east|west|Okafor was already in the East Wing and ran toward the paintings, which hang in the West Wing. The sound came from the west.]] and ran toward the paintings.

The window of Gallery 4 had been smashed from outside, and glass lay scattered across the [[lawn|floor|A window smashed from outside sprays glass inward, and Okafor later cuts her hand on shards from the gallery floor.]]. Three frames hung empty on the north wall: two small landscapes and a portrait of a woman in blue.

I radioed the police at 23:20. While I waited I cut my hand picking shards off the gallery floor. Somewhere behind me the clocks in the East Wing chimed the half hour, each a little out of step with the others.

Police arrived at 23:40, [[forty|twenty-five|Glass broke at 23:15 and police arrived at 23:40. That is twenty-five minutes, not forty.]] minutes after I first heard the glass. Of the [[four|three|Three frames hung empty: two landscapes and one portrait. That makes three paintings.]] stolen paintings, the detective was most interested in the portrait. She asked who else had keys to the West Wing. Only the director and I do.

title: Log of the Marigold
genre: a ship's log over three days
paras: Log of the fishing boat Marigold, kept by skipper Edda Lunn.

Monday. Left Carrow harbour at 05:00 with a crew of four: myself, my son Piet, old Haldor and the new deckhand, Sefa. The wind was from the north. We ran [[north|south|The wind was from the north and at their backs, so they sailed south. That's why the trip home was "straight into that same north wind".]] with it at our backs toward the cod grounds.

Tuesday. Hauled the nets twice before noon. The first haul brought up forty fish. The second brought only [[thirty|twenty|The market bought "all sixty fish, forty of them from that first haul", so the second haul was twenty.]]. That made sixty in all, our best day this month. Sefa was sick over the side both times but kept working, which I respect.

Wednesday. Fog so thick I could not see the bow from the wheel. We lay at anchor, and all [[five|four|The crew is four: Edda, Piet, Haldor and Sefa ("a crew of four"), and "all four of us" come home.]] of us played cards in the cabin until 14:00, when it lifted. Haldor says he has seen worse fog in August than in any winter, and I believe him.

Thursday. Turned for home, straight into that same north wind. We left the grounds at 06:00. Tacking all the way, it took us nine hours instead of the usual five. We tied up in Carrow at [[13|15|Leaving at 06:00 and sailing for nine hours gets them in at 15:00, "half an hour before the fish market closed at 15:30".]]:00, half an hour before the fish market closed at 15:30. The market bought all sixty fish, forty of them from that first haul. All four of us were glad to be home.

title: Gran Ottilie's Plum Cake
genre: a handwritten family recipe card with notes
paras: Gran Ottilie's Plum Cake. Makes one cake, enough for eight slices.
You need twelve plums, halved and stoned. Cream 200 grams of butter with 200 grams of sugar until pale, then beat in three eggs, one at a time. Fold in 250 grams of flour and a pinch of salt.

Spread the batter in the square tin, not the round one. The plums need to sit in neat rows of six. Press the halves in cut side up, [[five|four|Twelve plums make twenty-four halves, and in rows of six that's four rows, not five.]] rows of six.

Put the [[round|square|The card says "the square tin, not the round one", and Mother says Gran "always used that square tin".]] tin on the middle shelf. Bake for [[forty|fifty|The halfway timer is "twenty-five minutes", and Gran "always baked it for exactly fifty minutes".]] minutes at 180 degrees. Halfway through the baking, turn the tin so the back browns evenly. A kitchen timer set for twenty-five minutes helps.

Note from Mother: Gran always used that square tin, and she always baked it for exactly fifty minutes. She cut it into [[six|eight|The cake is "enough for eight slices", one each for "the eight of us".]] pieces. That was one slice each for the eight of us at Sunday tea. She said the eggs must be at room temperature, and she was right; cold eggs make the butter split.

title: Brenner Hut Visitors’ Book
paras: Brenner Hut visitors' book. Six bunks, one stove, no water after October. Please leave dry wood for the next party.

12 September. Came up from Talla village by the south path. Red markers the whole way, so impossible to get lost, though it took us four hours and the sign at the bottom promises three. There are only two of us, so plenty of room in the [[eight|six|The hut has "Six bunks", and a party of five plus one lost walker filled them exactly.]] bunks. We left a full basket of wood.

14 September. A party of five from the coast. We took [[four|five|There were five in the party, and with six bunks that left exactly one, "the last one", for the walker.]] of the bunks and gave the last one to a lost walker who came in at dusk. The wood basket was full, so thank you, whoever you were.

[[13|15|The lost walker reached the hut at dusk on 14 September and says so ("turned up on the 14th"), so this entry can't be dated before then.]] September. Me again, the lost walker who turned up on the 14th. I came up the north path by mistake instead of the south path from Talla. The [[south|north|The south path from Talla has "Red markers the whole way". The unmarked one, where the walker got lost, is the north path.]] path is shorter, but it has no markers at all.
20 September. Snow already. Only one bunk had a blanket left. Whoever took the other five, please bring them back.

title: Show Report: The Glass Orchard
genre: a theatre stage manager's show report
paras: Show Report: The Glass Orchard, performance 12 of 20. Stage manager: Wren Abara.

Timing. Curtain up at 19:32, two minutes late because of a queue at the bar. Act One ran 55 minutes. The interval ran 20 minutes. Act Two began at 20:[[37|47|Curtain at 19:32 plus 55 minutes of Act One and a 20-minute interval makes 20:47. A 75-minute Act Two ending at 22:02 agrees.]] and ran 75 minutes, a little long because of the duel. The show came down at 22:02.

Props. The wooden sword snapped during the duel in Act [[One|Two|The duel is what made Act Two run long, and it is "the last scene of the play".]]. Teodor finished the fight with a candlestick. The audience laughed, which they should not have, since it is the last scene of the play. A new sword is ordered for Thursday.

Cast. Mira Holt was off sick, so her understudy, Jonah Fell, played the Gardener. [[Mira|Jonah|Mira was "off sick" and "hopes to be back", so it was Jonah who went on and was word-perfect.]] was word-perfect. Mira hopes to be back for Thursday.

House. We sold 340 seats out of 400. That left [[80|60|400 seats minus 340 sold leaves 60, which is exactly the empty balcony.]] seats empty. The stalls were full; nobody at all sat in the balcony, which holds exactly 60.

title: Letter to the Landlord
genre: a tenant's letter to a landlord about repairs
paras: Dear Ms Varga,

I am writing again about flat 3B, on the third floor. The boiler has not worked since Monday the 4th. Today is Monday the [[12th|11th|The boiler broke on Monday the 4th, so the following Monday is the 11th, as Wednesday the 6th and Saturday the 9th confirm.]], so that is a full week without hot water.

Your plumber, Gustav, came on Wednesday the 6th. He said the part would take [[five|three|Gustav came on Wednesday the 6th and the part was due on Saturday the 9th: three days, not five.]] days to arrive. That would have been Saturday the 9th, and it did not come.

Meanwhile the lift is broken too, so I carry the shopping up to the [[fourth|third|Flat 3B is "on the third floor", as the signature says too.]] floor every day. The kitchen window still will not close either, and the nights are getting cold.
I paid the rent on the 1st as always. I would be grateful if all [[four|three|There are three problems: the boiler, the lift and the kitchen window.]] repairs could be done this week.
Yours sincerely,
Ilse Brandt, flat 3B, third floor

title: Reptile House Feeding Log
paras: Feeding log, Reptile House. Keeper on duty: Amos Kerr.
07:00. The two tortoises, Basil and Mo, had their greens. Basil ate everything. Mo left the kale, as usual.

08:30. Fed the [[four|three|One leg each used "three legs", and Pip is "the largest of the three".]] young crocodiles one chicken leg each. That is three legs gone. The largest of the three, Pip, snapped at the tongs again. Please use the long tongs with [[Mo|Pip|Pip is the crocodile that "snapped at the tongs". Mo is one of the two tortoises.]].
11:00. The python refused her monthly meal. She is due to shed soon, and snakes often refuse food before a shed, so there is no need to worry.

14:00. [[Basil|Mo|Basil "ate everything" this morning. It was Mo who left the kale, and now both tortoises are fully fed.]] finally ate the kale left in the enclosure this morning. Both tortoises are now fully fed.

16:00. Counted six chicken legs left in the fridge and ordered more. Six is enough for [[three|two|Three crocodiles at one leg each get through "three legs" a day, so the "six chicken legs left" last two days.]] more days of crocodile meals.

title: Diary, Saturday
paras: Saturday, my fourteenth birthday

Worst birthday ever, and you only turn fourteen once. Mum forgot the candles, so Dad stuck [[thirteen|fourteen|It's "my fourteenth birthday", and "you only turn fourteen once".]] matches in the cake instead. Gran laughed so hard she had to sit down on the stairs.

My brother Tobias, who is [[eight|nine|His card says "AGE 9", and he was five when the writer turned ten, five years younger than fourteen.]], gave me a rock. He says it's a meteorite. It is definitely from the garden. His card said FROM TOBIAS AGE 9, with the 9 backwards.

The party started at three. Lena was supposed to come at [[two|three|"The party started at three", and arriving at half past four made her "Ninety minutes late".]] like everyone else. She finally arrived at half past four because her bus broke down. Ninety minutes late! But she brought the best present: [[three|two|One ticket is for the writer and one for Lena, and Lena's mum is driving "us both".]] tickets to see The Velvet Moths next Friday. One is for me and one is for her.
So actually not the worst birthday. Second worst. The worst was turning ten, when Tobias, aged five, was sick on the bouncy castle.
Note to self: ask Mum if I can go on Friday. Lena's mum is driving us both.

title: Hollin Fell Weather Summary
paras: Hollin Fell Weather Station: summary for the week ending Sunday.

Rain fell on [[five|four|It rained on Monday, Tuesday, Thursday and Saturday, and the other three days "stayed dry". That's four wet days.]] days this week. It rained on Monday, Tuesday, Thursday and Saturday. Wednesday, Friday and Sunday stayed dry.

The wettest day was [[Monday|Tuesday|"Monday brought 6", and "Monday's 6 millimetres all fell before breakfast". The 18 belongs to Tuesday, the one rainy day otherwise missing.]], with 18 millimetres. Monday brought 6, Thursday 4 and Saturday 2. That makes a weekly total of [[32|30|18 + 6 + 4 + 2 makes 30, and the field note says "at 30".]] millimetres. Monday's 6 millimetres all fell before breakfast. The lower field floods at 25 in a week, so at 30 it was under water by Friday.
The warmest afternoon was Friday at 21 degrees, and the coldest night was Wednesday at 3 degrees. The wind blew mostly from the west.

The station cat, Barometer, was found asleep in the rain gauge on [[Thursday|Friday|Thursday was a rainy day, while Friday "stayed dry", which is why no harm was done.]]. As it was a dry day, no harm was done. Next week looks drier, with rain forecast only for Tuesday.

title: Hotel Marisol Lost Property
genre: a lost-and-found report at a seaside hotel
paras: Hotel Marisol, lost property report, written by night porter Duma Okoye.

I came on duty at 23:30 and started my rounds. The bar staff locked up at 23:35. I found a brown leather suitcase behind the lounge piano at 23:[[50|40|Okoye came on duty at 23:30 and found it "ten minutes into my shift", five minutes after the bar "locked up at 23:35": 23:40.]]. That was ten minutes into my shift, and five minutes after the bar closed.

The label reads Ruth Kessler, room 214. Nobody called Kessler is staying with us. Room [[241|214|The label says "room 214", and the phone call asks about "a case left in room 214".]] has been empty since Tuesday, when the Lund family checked out.

Contents: three blue shirts, a pair of boots, a book of crosswords with every puzzle finished, and a seashell wrapped in a sock. One shirt is missing a button; the other [[three|two|There are "three blue shirts", one is missing a button, and Okoye "folded all three back in". That leaves two.]] are fine. I folded all three back in neatly.

I locked the case in the luggage room. It is the only [[black|brown|The case found behind the piano is "a brown leather suitcase", and all the others in the luggage room are black.]] case in there; all the others are black.
At 06:00 Missus Lund telephoned from the station. She asked whether anyone had found a case left in room 214. Her mother, she said, is Ruth Kessler. Mystery solved, I think.

title: Dunmoor Castle Tour Script
genre: a castle tour guide's script with notes
paras: Good morning, and welcome to Dunmoor Castle. The tour starts here at 10:00. It lasts forty minutes, so we will finish in the gift shop at 10:[[45|40|The tour starts at 10:00 and lasts forty minutes, and the guide's note says the group "must be out by 10:40".]].
Dunmoor was built in 1312 by Lord Aldric Moor. When he died, the castle passed to his only child, Isobel, who held it through the great siege.

The siege lasted forty days. Isobel commanded the defence from the top of the tower. To keep her soldiers fed, [[Aldric|Isobel|Aldric had died before the siege. The castle passed to Isobel, who "commanded the defence", so the order was hers.]] had the horses killed for meat, then the dogs. On the [[thirtieth|fortieth|The siege "lasted forty days", so the last day was the fortieth, as the note about "forty days" confirms.]] and last day, the story goes, they threw a fresh fish over the wall to show they were not starving. The attackers gave up the next morning.
Note to guide: forty days, the same as the tour lasts in minutes. Children like that.

This is the Great Hall. Count the fireplaces. There are three. Aldric built one for each of his [[four|three|There are three fireplaces, one per brother, and the guide's note says "three brothers, three fireplaces".]] brothers, who all lived here.
Note to guide: three brothers, three fireplaces, easy for children to remember. If we are running late, skip the tower. We must be out by 10:40 for the next group.
